title: Effects of Pregnancy on Oral Health: A Narrative Review.
research_objective: To explore the factors responsible for oral health conditions during pregnancy and to recommend comprehensive management strategies.
main_findings: Changes in immunological response, oral environment, increased levels of steroid hormones, and nutritional deficits contribute to oral health conditions during pregnancy. Untreated periodontal diseases during pregnancy are associated with adverse maternal and fetal outcomes. Salivary changes in pregnant women exacerbate dental caries.
safety_information: The second trimester is recommended for dental procedures to ensure optimal maternal and fetal health.
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported in the abstract
future_research: Develop targeted interventions and innovative solutions for delivering oral health education and preventive care to pregnant women.
summary: The abstract discusses the impact of pregnancy on oral health, highlighting the need for comprehensive management strategies, including prevention, patient education, and safe management of existing conditions. It also emphasizes the importance of collaboration between dental professionals and prenatal care providers.

title: Feasibility of 5-Aminolevulenic Acid Fluorescence for Diagnostic Guidance in Intracranial Lymphoma Surgery: A Case Series and Systematic Review of 170 Patients.
research_objective: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of 5-ALA-guided biopsy in adult patients with radiologically suspected intracranial lymphoma and to assess the relationship between corticosteroid use and 5-ALA fluorescence patterns.
main_findings: 5-ALA fluorescence was observed in 77.6% of 18 studies (170 patients), with 78% pooled sensitivity and 22% false-negative rate. In the institutional series, 5-ALA fluorescence was strong in 4 out of 5 patients, with an overall positive predictive value of 80%. Corticosteroid use did not uniformly suppress fluorescence but may influence diagnostic reliability.
efficacy_information: 5-ALA fluorescence serves as a useful adjunct for intracranial lymphoma biopsy, enhancing sampling efficiency and procedural safety. However, fluorescence alone cannot ensure diagnostic adequacy, and frozen section confirmation remains necessary.
explicit_limitations: Fluorescence alone cannot ensure diagnostic adequacy, and frozen section confirmation remains necessary.
future_research: Recommendations for future research include further studies to determine the optimal corticosteroid use and to explore the potential of 5-ALA fluorescence in combination with other diagnostic tools.
summary: The study found that 5-ALA fluorescence is useful for guiding biopsy in intracranial lymphoma, but its efficacy is not absolute. Corticosteroid use does not uniformly suppress fluorescence but may influence diagnostic reliability. Future research is needed to optimize corticosteroid use and to combine 5-ALA fluorescence with other diagnostic methods.

title: Resurgence of Acquired Syphilitic Uveitis: Characteristics, Challenges and Outcomes.
research_objective: To characterize the clinical, imaging features, treatment modalities, and outcomes of syphilitic uveitis (SU) at a tertiary-care center in North India over the last decade.
main_findings: The study included 26 patients (44 eyes) with syphilitic uveitis, predominantly male with a mean age of 37.9 ± 12.1 years. The majority of patients (50%) were co-infected with HIV. The most common forms of syphilitic uveitis were posterior uveitis (61.4%) and panuveitis (36.4%). Initial misdiagnosis occurred in 38.5% of cases, and corticosteroids were empirically used in these cases. Definitive treatment included intravenous ceftriaxone or aqueous penicillin with adjunctive corticosteroids in a few cases. At a median follow-up of 9 months, 93.2% of eyes showed resolution, and 54.5% achieved best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) ≥20/30. Factors associated with favorable outcomes included better initial vision, posterior uveitis, and treatment with aqueous penicillin.
efficacy_information: Definitive treatment with intravenous ceftriaxone or aqueous penicillin with adjunctive corticosteroids was effective in achieving resolution in 93.2% of eyes and BCVA ≥20/30 in 54.5% of eyes.
safety_information: Corticosteroids were empirically used in 38.5% of cases, and aqueous penicillin was used in definitive treatment.
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported
future_research: Recommendations for future research include further evaluation of aqueous penicillin as a treatment modality.
summary: The study found syphilitic uveitis to be prevalent, especially in the post-COVID era, with favorable outcomes achieved with intravenous ceftriaxone or aqueous penicillin in combination with corticosteroids.

title: Advances in the characterization of in vitro-generated red blood cells: from biophysical properties to functional applications.
research_objective: To integrate multi-omics platforms to comprehensively profile the developmental and functional states of in vitro-generated red blood cells (RBCs) and to provide a translational framework for their development and evaluation.
main_findings: The review highlights the challenges in recapitulating erythropoiesis in vitro, emphasizing the need for a systems-level perspective that integrates multi-omics data. It underscores the importance of clarifying mechanisms behind incomplete enucleation and hemoglobin switching to optimize the manufacture of in vitro-generated RBCs. The review also discusses translational applications such as transfusion medicine, rare blood type management, disease modeling, and drug delivery, along with safety, ethical, and regulatory considerations.
explicit_limitations: The review outlines the challenges in characterizing in vitro-generated RBCs, including the difficulty in recapitulating erythropoiesis in vitro and the need for a systems-level perspective that integrates multi-omics data.
future_research: The review proposes a translational framework that integrates multi-omics data into the development and evaluation of in vitro-generated RBCs, and it discusses translational applications such as transfusion medicine, rare blood type management, disease modeling, and drug delivery, along with safety, ethical, and regulatory considerations.
summary: The review emphasizes the need for a comprehensive approach to characterize in vitro-generated red blood cells (RBCs) using multi-omics platforms. It highlights the challenges in achieving functional performance and discusses translational applications and considerations for clinical readiness.

title: A scoping review and comprehensive needs assessment for developing an intergenerational cognitive and physical activity program for MCI patients and their adult children.
research_objective: Identify cognitive, physical, and psychosocial challenges experienced by MCI patients and explore the needs, preferences, barriers, and facilitators regarding participation in an intergenerational PA+CA program.
main_findings: Highlights challenges such as memory loss, fatigue, social withdrawal, and a desire for meaningful, safe, and structured activities. Identifies barriers including overload, physical limitations, and time constraints. Identifies facilitators such as routine, emotional support, and family connection.
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported in the abstract
future_research: Offer guidance for designing effective intergenerational PA+CA programs.
summary: This study identified challenges and facilitators for intergenerational PA+CA programs for MCI patients and their adult children, providing insights for program design and future research.

title: Semiflex-assisted vacuum therapy for perianal fistulas: the Semiflex pilot study.
research_objective: To evaluate the feasibility and clinical applicability of the Semiflex catheter in perianal fistula management
main_findings: Semiflex therapy was feasible in a subset of patients and allowed outpatient treatment. However, maintaining vacuum and achieving long-term fistula closure remains challenging. While Semiflex may have a role in perianal fistula management, further research is needed to refine patient selection and optimize its application.
efficacy_information: Clinical fistula closure was observed in 50% of patients, but none showed radiological healing at 3 months.
safety_information: One serious adverse event occurred, requiring early treatment discontinuation, while minor complications, including local skin reactions and pressure sores, were managed conservatively.
explicit_limitations: Maintaining vacuum and achieving long-term fistula closure remains challenging. While Semiflex may have a role in perianal fistula management, further research is needed to refine patient selection and optimize its application.
future_research: Further research is needed to refine patient selection and optimize the application of the Semiflex catheter in perianal fistula management.

title: Dexmedetomidine nasal spray for acute agitation in adults with bipolar disorder: a single-arm open-label trial.
research_objective: To explore the feasibility, preliminary tolerability, and within-subject changes in agitation severity with dexmedetomidine nasal spray in bipolar disorder patients with acute agitation.
main_findings: The study found that dexmedetomidine nasal spray was well tolerated, with a response rate of 75% for a ≥40% reduction in the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale-Excited Component (PEC) total score at 2 hours post-treatment. The mean change from baseline in the PEC total score at 2 hours post-dose was -7.3 (4.5). Observed symptom relief began as early as 10 minutes after medication. The most common adverse events were hypotension, hypertension, decreased heart rate, and increased heart rate.
efficacy_information: The response rate (≥40% PEC reduction) was 75% at 2 hours post-treatment.
safety_information: The most common adverse events included hypotension, hypertension, decreased heart rate, and increased heart rate.
explicit_limitations: The study was a single-center single-arm, open-label study with a small sample size of 20 patients.
future_research: Larger randomized controlled trials are needed to establish safety, efficacy, and generalizability.
summary: This early-phase study found that dexmedetomidine nasal spray was well tolerated and reduced agitation severity in bipolar disorder patients with acute agitation, with a response rate of 75% at 2 hours post-treatment. However, larger trials are needed to confirm these findings.

title: Surface Hopping with Fully Correlated Methods.
research_objective: Analyze the current status of fully correlated electronic structure methods in surface hopping simulations of fulvene and pyrrole.
main_findings: Fully correlated methods improve the description of bond rearrangements and hot ground-state dynamics in surface hopping simulations, while partially correlated approaches such as ADC(2) and TDDFT are sufficient for photophysical excited-state relaxation.
explicit_limitations: Persistent limitations such as active-space instabilities and potential-energy discontinuities imply the need for improved approaches.
future_research: Expanding the use of generalized active spaces in the short term and advancing large active space algorithms in the long term will be crucial for making high-accuracy nonadiabatic simulations broadly reliable and accessible.
summary: The abstract discusses the use of fully correlated electronic structure methods in surface hopping simulations of fulvene and pyrrole, highlighting their benefits and limitations, and recommends future research directions.

explicit_limitations: Challenges such as data heterogeneity, limited interpretability of AI models, and ethical issues in data sharing continue to impede clinical translation.
future_research: Future progress will rely on explainable AI, federated learning, and standardized data frameworks to promote transparency, reproducibility, and applicability in precision medicine.
summary: The abstract highlights the transition from traditional microbiome research methods to advanced computational tools that integrate multiomics data, enabling deeper insights into microbial communities and their roles in health and disease. However, challenges remain, and future research will focus on addressing these issues to facilitate clinical translation.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Microwave and Radiofrequency Ablation in the Treatment of Hyperparathyroidism in Older Individuals: A Multicenter Prospective Study.
research_objective: To compare the efficacy and safety of microwave ablation (MWA) and radiofrequency ablation (RFA) in older individuals with primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) and secondary hyperparathyroidism (SHPT).
main_findings: The overall cure rate for primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) was 80% (61 of 76; 78% for MWA vs 86% for RFA; P = .59). The PTH achievement rate for secondary hyperparathyroidism (SHPT) was 90% (69 of 77; 92% for MWA vs 87% for RFA; P = .48). Both techniques reduced serum PTH, calcium, and ALP between baseline and 24 months in PHPT and SHPT, whereas phosphorus increased in PHPT and decreased in SHPT. Preoperative PTH level was the only independent predictor of treatment failure.
efficacy_information: The overall cure rate for PHPT was 80% (61 of 76; 78% for MWA vs 86% for RFA; P = .59). The PTH achievement rate for SHPT was 90% (69 of 77; 92% for MWA vs 87% for RFA; P = .48).
safety_information: The most common complication was transient hypocalcemia (13% in PHPT; 51% in SHPT). There was no evidence of a difference in complication rate for MWA versus RFA in participants with PHPT (15% [eight of 54] vs 27% [six of 22]; P = .21) or SHPT (92% [36 of 39] vs 87% [33 of 38]; P = .48).
explicit_limitations: Selection bias was minimized using inverse probability weighting.
future_research: Predictors of treatment failure were identified through univariable and multivariable analyses.
summary: In older individuals with hyperparathyroidism, microwave ablation (MWA) and radiofrequency ablation (RFA) were found to be safe and effective alternatives, with preoperative PTH level being the only independent predictor of treatment failure. Both techniques reduced serum PTH, calcium, and ALP, while phosphorus levels changed in both hyperparathyroidism types. No significant differences were observed in complication rates between MWA and RFA.

title: Radiological Management of Chyle Leaks Following Oesophagectomy: A Systematic Review.
research_objective: To systematically review the literature on the efficacy, safety, and clinical outcomes of radiological interventions for managing chyle leaks following oesophagectomy.
main_findings: Radiological interventions, particularly lymphangiography with or without thoracic duct embolisation (TDE) or thoracic duct disruption (TDD), are safe, minimally invasive, and increasingly effective alternatives to surgical ligation for managing chyle leaks after oesophagectomy. Lymphangiography alone was often both diagnostic and therapeutic, with some studies reporting cure rates of up to 70%. Complications were uncommon and generally minor.
efficacy_information: Radiological interventions, particularly lymphangiography with or without TDE/TDD, are safe, minimally invasive, and increasingly effective alternatives to surgical ligation for managing chyle leaks after oesophagectomy. Lymphangiography alone was often both diagnostic and therapeutic, with some studies reporting cure rates of up to 70%. Complications were uncommon and generally minor.
safety_information: Radiological interventions, particularly lymphangiography with or without TDE/TDD, are safe, minimally invasive, and increasingly effective alternatives to surgical ligation for managing chyle leaks after oesophagectomy. Lymphangiography alone was often both diagnostic and therapeutic, with some studies reporting cure rates of up to 70%. Complications were uncommon and generally minor.
explicit_limitations: The literature is limited by heterogeneity, small sample sizes, and predominance of retrospective designs.
future_research: Further prospective studies and standardised reporting are required to establish radiological intervention as the gold standard of management in chyle leak and to define its role relative to surgery.
summary: Radiological interventions, particularly lymphangiography with or without thoracic duct embolisation or disruption, are effective and safe alternatives to surgical ligation for managing chyle leaks after oesophagectomy, with some studies reporting cure rates up to 70%. However, the literature is limited by heterogeneity, small sample sizes, and predominance of retrospective designs, necessitating further prospective studies and standardised reporting.

main_findings: Changes in epitope-site sequence may alter glycosylation patterns at antigenic sites, potentially affecting the virus' efficiency to induce an immune response.

title: The Effects of COVID-19 on Voice.
research_objective: To explore the multifaceted nature of dysphonia associated with COVID-19, arising from both direct and indirect consequences of the pandemic.
main_findings: Prevalence rates of dysphonia among COVID-19 patients range widely from 25% to 79%, with significant underreporting. Factors contributing to voice changes include laryngeal inflammation, respiratory function impairment, treatment-related interventions, and increased vocal strain from masking and virtual communication. Professional voice users, such as teachers and singers, experienced unique challenges, including increased voice fatigue and apprehension regarding aerosol transmission during singing. Innovations with voice also emerged, utilizing artificial intelligence voice analysis for COVID-19 detection.
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported in the abstract
future_research: Continued research is necessary to further delineate the long-term implications and optimal treatment approaches for those affected.
summary: This study explores the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on vocal health, including prevalence rates of dysphonia, contributing factors, and emerging innovations. It highlights the unique challenges faced by professional voice users and the need for further research to understand long-term effects.

title: Nanophotonics in Molecular Imaging and Biomedicine: Diagnostics, Therapies, and Translational Challenges.
research_objective: To review core nanophotonic principles and their applications in molecular imaging, diagnostics, and therapy guidance within biological systems.
main_findings: The review outlines core nanophotonic principles, including surface plasmon resonance, optical confinement, and photon-matter interactions, which underpin emerging molecular imaging probes and diagnostic tools. Biocompatible nanomaterials such as quantum dots, gold nanoparticles, and photonic metamaterials enable highly sensitive, selective imaging and biosensing for early, minimally invasive disease detection and monitoring. Targeted photothermal and photodynamic therapies using near-infrared (NIR) and NIR-II light advance image-guided interventions, allowing deeper tissue penetration with minimal collateral damage. The integration of nanophotonic components into lab-on-a-chip and microfluidic platforms for point-of-care diagnostics is discussed. Machine learning is highlighted for enhancing molecular imaging analysis and probe optimization, enabling real-time data interpretation and predictive modeling tailored to patient-specific profiles.
explicit_limitations: Challenges remain in biocompatibility, light penetration, scalability, and regulatory approval.
future_research: Future research is recommended to address biocompatibility, light penetration, scalability, and regulatory approval challenges.
summary: This review discusses the advancements in nanophotonic principles and their applications in molecular imaging, diagnostics, and therapy guidance, emphasizing the integration of machine learning for personalized medicine.

main_findings: The mean pooled improvement in adherence was found to be 18% and the most effective tool was the digital therapeutics app discussed in Li et al's study. Smartphones and apps enhance coronary artery disease management by promoting medication compliance.

explicit_limitations: Challenges include data security and smartphone usage among the elderly.

title: A Systematic Review of Population Pharmacokinetics, Safety, and Factors Influencing Trough Concentrations of Voriconazole in Asian Patients with Liver Dysfunction.
research_objective: To systematically review recent research on voriconazole (VRC) use in Asian patients with liver dysfunction to provide a scientific basis for individualized therapy.
main_findings: The study included 14 studies covering safety, factors affecting VRC trough concentrations, and population pharmacokinetic characteristics in Asian patients with liver dysfunction. The most common adverse drug reactions (ADRs) were hepatotoxicity, neurotoxicity, and visual impairment, occurring within 7 days of VRC administration. VRC trough concentrations are influenced by liver impairment severity, CYP2C19 polymorphisms, and albumin and bilirubin levels. Population pharmacokinetic models showed a significant reduction in clearance (CL) among patients with Child-Pugh (CP) classification C, with a significant prolongation in the elimination half-life (t₁/2) for CP-C patients.
safety_information: The study reported adverse drug reactions (ADRs) such as hepatotoxicity, neurotoxicity, and visual impairment, which typically occurred within 7 days of VRC administration.
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported in the abstract
future_research: Therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) and population pharmacokinetic (PPK) studies can aid in optimizing VRC dosing, ensuring safer and more effective individualized therapy.
summary: This study reviews recent research on voriconazole use in Asian patients with liver dysfunction, identifying common adverse drug reactions and influencing factors on trough concentrations. It suggests the use of therapeutic drug monitoring and population pharmacokinetic studies to optimize dosing for safer and more effective treatment.

title: Menopausal Hormone Therapy-Risks, Benefits and Emerging Options: A Narrative Review.
research_objective: Synthesize contemporary evidence on the benefits, risks, and emerging options in menopausal hormone therapy (MHT), emphasizing the last five years of literature.
main_findings: MHT provides effective relief for vasomotor symptoms and is the first-line treatment for genitourinary syndrome of menopause. It prevents early postmenopausal bone loss and reduces fractures in selected cases. Cardiovascular prevention is not an indication. MHT effects on breast cancer risks are regimen-specific, with neutral to favorable outcomes with estrogen-alone after hysterectomy and increasing with longer use of combined therapy. MHT confers modest improvements in sleep, mood, intercourse, and quality of life. Estetrol (E4) shows anti-VMS efficacy and favorable pharmacology, but its long-term cardiovascular, thrombotic, and breast safety data are pending.
efficacy_information: MHT is effective for vasomotor symptoms, genitourinary syndrome of menopause, and bone loss prevention.
safety_information: MHT is associated with higher risks of venous thromboembolism and stroke with oral regimens, particularly those using conjugated equine estrogens. The risk also varies by the type of progestogen used. MHT can increase breast cancer risks with combined therapy. The absolute risk of ovarian cancer is small, but evidence for colorectal cancer is mixed. MHT can improve sleep, mood, intercourse, and quality of life.
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported in the abstract.
future_research: Individualized MHT based on patient, timing, route, dose, and choice of progestogen is recommended. Further research is needed on the long-term cardiovascular, thrombotic, and breast safety of MHT, especially with E4.
summary: This study synthesizes recent literature on menopausal hormone therapy, highlighting its efficacy for vasomotor symptoms, genitourinary syndrome of menopause, and bone loss prevention. However, it also identifies risks such as increased thrombotic and breast cancer risks, particularly with combined therapy. Future research is needed to address these risks and to evaluate the long-term safety of MHT, especially with the use of estetrol (E4).

title: Use of snake antivenom in the Region of the Americas: a systematic review.
research_objective: To evaluate the use of antivenom therapy in Bothrops envenomation in the Region of the Americas and to synthesize data on treatment outcomes, adverse reactions and long-term sequelae.
main_findings: Bothrops envenomations occurred more frequently in men, predominantly affected the lower limbs, and typically resulted in moderate-grade envenoming. Adverse reactions to antivenom therapy were common, with early reactions occurring in 19.6% of patients and delayed reactions in 1.6%. Individuals experienced clinical complications such as severe oedema, secondary infections, and coagulopathies. Some patients also experienced permanent sequelae, though these were relatively infrequent. For studies reporting on deaths, 0.8% of patients died.
efficacy_information: Antivenom therapy remains central to the management of Bothrops envenomation.
safety_information: Adverse reactions to antivenom therapy were common, with early reactions occurring in 19.6% of patients and delayed reactions in 1.6%. Individuals experienced clinical complications such as severe oedema, secondary infections, and coagulopathies. Some patients also experienced permanent sequelae, though these were relatively infrequent.
explicit_limitations: Substantial heterogeneity study methods and reported outcomes, precluded the ability to conduct pooled analyses and generalize findings.
future_research: Addressing these challenges requires ongoing research to strengthen antivenom manufacturing, explore adjunct therapies and improve post-envenomation care.
summary: The study found that antivenom therapy is essential for managing Bothrops envenomation, but it also highlighted common adverse reactions and complications. Future research is needed to improve antivenom quality and post-treatment care.

title: Nanoparticles Used for the Delivery of RNAi-Based Therapeutics.
research_objective: To review advances in non-viral nanocarriers for enhancing the clinical translation of RNA interference (RNAi) by addressing stability, immunogenicity, and endosomal escape issues.
main_findings: The review highlights advances in non-viral nanocarriers such as liposomes, polymeric nanoparticles, and extracellular vesicles (EVs) that stabilize nucleic acids, tune biodistribution, and enable tissue-selective delivery. These platforms have achieved tissue-selective uptake, traversed physiological barriers, and enhanced efficacy while maintaining favorable safety profiles across various disease areas.
efficacy_information: Achieved tissue-selective uptake, traversed physiological barriers, and enhanced efficacy while maintaining favorable safety profiles.
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported in the abstract.
future_research: Priorities include good manufacturing practice scale, consistent manufacture, especially for EVs; more efficient loading and cargo control; improved endosomal escape and biodistribution; and rigorous, long-term safety evaluation with standardized, head-to-head benchmarking. Emerging directions such as in vivo EVs biogenesis, theragnostic integration, and data-driven formulation discovery are poised to accelerate translation.
summary: The review discusses advancements in non-viral nanocarriers for RNA interference, highlighting their ability to stabilize nucleic acids, enhance delivery, and maintain safety profiles. These platforms are being used across various disease areas and are poised for further development and clinical translation.

title: Comparative Risk of Gallstone Formation After Sleeve Gastrectomy and Roux-En-Y Gastric Bypass: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
research_objective: To compare the risk of gallstone formation after sleeve gastrectomy (SG) versus Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB)
main_findings: SG was associated with a lower risk of gallstone formation than RYGB, with a pooled odds ratio (OR) of 0.68 (95% CI 0.53-0.88) and a p-value of 0.003. The protective association was evident in studies with < 2 years of follow-up but not in ≥ 2-year follow-up.
efficacy_information: The protective association was evident in studies with < 2 years of follow-up (OR 0.59, 95% CI 0.42-0.82; I²=46%).
explicit_limitations: Standardized outcome definitions, longer follow-up, and stratification by UDCA use are needed to refine comparative risk estimates.
future_research: Standardized outcome definitions, longer follow-up, and stratification by UDCA use are needed to refine comparative risk estimates.
summary: The study found that sleeve gastrectomy (SG) is associated with a lower risk of gallstone formation compared to Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB), particularly in the short-term. However, the results are heterogeneous and sensitive to study weight.

title: Efficacy and safety of traditional Chinese exercises in cardiac rehabilitation of patients after percutaneous coronary intervention: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
research_objective: To explore the efficacy and safety of traditional Chinese exercise (TCE) on cardiac rehabilitation in patients after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).
main_findings: The study found that TCE therapy, including Baduanjin, Tai Chi, Wuqinxi, and Yi Jinjing, combined with conventional treatment and/or exercise, was superior to conventional treatment and/or exercise alone in reducing the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), improving left ventricular ejection fraction, NT-ProBNP levels, six-minute walk distance, left ventricular end diastolic diameter, left ventricular end-systolic diameter, VO2 max, anaerobic threshold, metabolite equivalents, Seattle Angina Questionnaire scores, and short form 36 Health Survey questionnaire scores. However, there was no significant difference in VO2 peak between the treatment and control groups.
efficacy_information: The study found that TCE therapy may have efficacy in reducing the incidence of MACE, improving cardiac function, exercise endurance, and quality of life in patients after PCI.
safety_information: The study did not report any specific safety information.
explicit_limitations: Methodological quality was of high risk of bias in blinding of participants and personnel, and unclear of bias in blinding of outcome assessment and allocation concealment.
future_research: The study recommends further research to explore the efficacy and safety of TCE therapy combined with conventional treatment and/or exercise in patients after PCI.
summary: This study found that TCE therapy, when combined with conventional treatment and/or exercise, may be effective in reducing MACE incidence, improving cardiac function, exercise endurance, and quality of life in patients after PCI, but the efficacy of VO2 peak was not significantly different from conventional treatment and/or exercise alone.

title: [Resection of soft tissue sarcomas on the thigh].
research_objective: Complete tumor resection while maintaining oncologically required safety margins, with a focus on functional limb preservation.
main_findings: The outcomes of soft tissue sarcoma resection in the thigh are generally favorable, both oncologically and functionally. Early diagnosis and treatment in specialized centers can improve survival and reduce the amputation rate.
explicit_limitations: Tumors that are not surgically accessible. Advanced or progressive tumors with extensive metastases and short life expectancy. Complete postoperative loss of function of the extremity.
future_research: Not reported in the abstract
summary: The study reports favorable outcomes for soft tissue sarcoma resection in the thigh, emphasizing the importance of early diagnosis and treatment in specialized centers. It also outlines limitations for surgical accessibility and patient condition.

title: Management and outcome variability in hernia-related small bowel obstruction: insights from the SnapSBO study.
research_objective: To explore the management and outcomes of hernia-related small bowel obstruction (hSBO) for patients captured in the European Society for Trauma and Emergency Surgery (ESTES) SnapSBO database.
main_findings: The study found that parastomal hernia management led to the highest complication rate and prolonged postoperative length of stay compared to other hernia types. Functional recovery was significantly worse in patients with parastomal hernia than in those with incisional or primary inguinal hernias.
safety_information: Parastomal hernia management was associated with higher complication rates and longer hospital stays.
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported in the abstract
future_research: Future research should focus on patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) and develop evidence-based, context-specific guidelines for hSBO management.
summary: The study analyzed hSBO management in a European database and found that parastomal hernias are associated with higher complications and longer hospital stays, highlighting the need for further research and guidelines.

title: Non-Protein-Coding RNA and Acute Kidney Injury: New Developments from Pathogenesis to Potential Biomarker.
research_objective: To provide a comprehensive overview of the involvement of non-coding RNA, in particular microRNAs, in the early diagnosis and therapeutic strategies for Acute Kidney Injury (AKI).
main_findings: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) have shown the ability to detect AKI earlier than traditional biomarkers like serum creatinine, offering the potential to enhance clinical decision-making.
explicit_limitations: Further clinical studies and translational applications are still needed to validate these findings and implement them in patient care.
future_research: Further clinical studies and translational applications are still needed to validate these findings and implement them in patient care.
summary: This review highlights the potential of microRNAs as sensitive biomarkers and novel treatment targets for AKI, aiming to improve clinical decision-making and reduce mortality rates.

title: Medication-related problems and contributing factors in patients with cardiovascular disorders in Ethiopia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
research_objective: To assess the prevalence of medication-related problems (MRPs) among cardiovascular disease (CVD) patients in Ethiopia.
main_findings: The pooled prevalence of MRPs among CVD patients in Ethiopia was 74% (95% CI 66-81), with an average of 1.65 MRPs per patient (95% CI 1.48-1.82). Common MRPs included patient noncompliance, ineffective drug therapy, and the need for additional drug therapy. Factors contributing to MRPs were identified as polypharmacy, poor involvement in therapeutic decisions, advanced age, the presence of comorbidities, and prolonged illness duration.
explicit_limitations: The study did not identify sample size or study period as significant sources of heterogeneity.
future_research: Healthcare providers should focus on individualized care, regular medication reviews, and patient education to address medication-related problems effectively.
summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis found a high prevalence of medication-related problems among CVD patients in Ethiopia, highlighting the need for targeted interventions to improve medication management and patient outcomes.

title: Cancer cell death: Cell-autonomous and immunogenic dimensions.
research_objective: Understanding the molecular determinants of regulated cell death (RCD) and immunogenic cell death (ICD) in cancer and their impact on immune responses and therapeutic efficacy.
main_findings: The abstract highlights the interconnected pathways of necroptosis, pyroptosis, ferroptosis, and apoptosis in shaping neoplastic transformation and tumor progression. It also emphasizes the importance of immunogenic cell death (ICD) in cancer therapy, which is characterized by the emission of immunomodulatory damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) from dying cancer cells. The balance between immunostimulatory and immunosuppressive DAMPs influences the effectiveness of adaptive immunity and the efficacy of cancer therapeutics, including those synergistic with immune checkpoint inhibitors.
efficacy_information: The abstract suggests that ICD provides mechanistic grounds for the durable efficacy of certain cancer therapeutics and underpins their synergy with immune checkpoint inhibitors.
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported in the abstract
future_research: Understanding the molecular determinants of RCD and ICD is reshaping oncology, allowing for an increasingly refined integration between cytotoxicity and durable anticancer immune responses.
summary: The abstract discusses the importance of regulated cell death (RCD) and immunogenic cell death (ICD) in cancer therapy, highlighting their role in shaping neoplastic transformation, tumor progression, and response to treatment.

title: Glyphosate Use in Crop Systems: Risks to Health and Sustainable Alternatives.
research_objective: Examine the mechanisms, effects, and broader impacts of glyphosate, including its environmental and health impacts, and its role in achieving Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
main_findings: Glyphosate's mechanisms of action, effects on crop production, environmental impacts (soil degradation, water contamination, biodiversity loss), and links to various human health concerns (metabolic, neurological, reproductive, and oncological disorders) are examined. The review also assesses glyphosate's role in hindering the achievement of SDGs, particularly those related to food security, health, access to clean water, and the protection of marine ecosystems. Potential alternatives to glyphosate-based weed control are discussed.
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported in the abstract
future_research: Potential alternatives to glyphosate-based weed control are discussed to promote sustainable agricultural practices.
summary: This review examines glyphosate's effects on crop production, environmental impacts, and its role in achieving SDGs, highlighting its potential to disrupt both environmental and human health. It also discusses potential alternatives to promote sustainable agricultural practices.

title: Systematic Review of Active Safety Surveillance of Vaccines and Medicines in Low- and Middle-Income Countries.
research_objective: Identify and assess existing active safety surveillance in low- and middle-income countries, including key features, strengths, and limitations.
main_findings: Active safety surveillance in low- and middle-income countries has made progress but still faces challenges. Key findings include the use of mobile technologies, multi-sectoral collaborations, and the need for flexibility to incorporate new vaccines. Gaps identified include small sample sizes, lack of sustainability, limited flexible surveillance, staffing challenges, and limited use of standard case definitions and digital technologies.
explicit_limitations: Small sample sizes, lack of sustainability, limited flexible surveillance, staffing challenges, and limited use of standard case definitions and digital technologies are identified as limitations.
future_research: The capture and management of safety data through harmonized digital tools that promote consistency in recording and reporting and cross-country collaborations are crucial in further strengthening active safety surveillance in low- and middle-income countries.
summary: This systematic review found that active safety surveillance in low- and middle-income countries is progressing but faces significant challenges, including small sample sizes, lack of sustainability, and limited use of digital tools. The review recommends the use of harmonized digital tools and cross-country collaborations to improve surveillance.

title: Flagellin as a Versatile Adjuvant Platform: Genetic Fusion Approaches for Next-Generation Vaccines.
research_objective: To present a comprehensive overview of vaccine design strategies employing genetic fusion of antigens to flagellin for protection against various infectious diseases.
main_findings: Genetic fusion of antigens to flagellin has been shown to enhance immune responses against the antigen, and flagellin-based delivery has enabled several vaccine candidates to enter clinical trials.
efficacy_information: Enhanced immune responses against the antigen
safety_information: Substantial advantages in safety profiles compared to conventional vaccines
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported
future_research: Not reported
summary: The abstract highlights the potential of flagellin-based vaccines for enhancing immune responses and entering clinical trials, but does not provide specific efficacy or safety data, nor does it mention any limitations or future research directions.

title: Moyamoya Disease: Epidemiology, Clinical Characteristics, Diagnosis, Physiopathology, and Treatment.
research_objective: To advance understanding of Moyamoya disease (MMD) with a focus on its genetic, immunological, and angiogenic components, and to explore diagnostic and treatment advancements.
main_findings: Advances in imaging and genetics have expanded understanding of MMD, highlighting its genetic heterogeneity and complex interplay of genetic predisposition, immune dysregulation, and abnormal angiogenesis. The identification of RNF213 as the major genetic determinant contributing to MMD susceptibility is noted. However, issues in diagnosis and treatment, including atypical early symptoms, lack of specific diagnostic tools, and unclear indications for surgical treatment, remain unresolved.
explicit_limitations: Issues in diagnosis and treatment, including atypical early symptoms, lack of specific diagnostic tools, and unclear indications for surgical treatment, are noted as unresolved issues.
future_research: Future studies integrating genomics, immune biology, and angiogenesis research may enable biomarker discovery, precision risk stratification, and the development of disease-modifying treatments to improve long-term outcomes.
summary: The abstract highlights the genetic and immunological complexities of Moyamoya disease (MMD), emphasizing the need for further research to improve diagnosis and treatment, particularly in addressing the lack of specific diagnostic tools and unclear surgical indications.

title: Preoperative and Intraoperative Imaging during Transvenous Lead Extraction.
research_objective: To determine a patient-centered risk assessment for transvenous lead extraction using a combination of clinical factors and imaging modalities.
main_findings: Predicting complex lead extractions, which may require powered tools or a femoral approach, is aided by pre-procedural imaging and clinical assessment. Procedural imaging during extraction can improve safety and identify complications rapidly.
safety_information: Procedural imaging during extraction can improve safety and identify complications rapidly.
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported in the abstract
future_research: Not reported in the abstract
summary: The abstract discusses the use of a combination of clinical factors and imaging modalities to assess the risk of transvenous lead extraction, and how pre-procedural imaging can improve safety during the procedure.

title: Legal Risks in Obstetrics and Gynecology.
research_objective: To reduce the probability of being sued by patients through compassion and thorough attention to patients, and to understand the role of medical and hospital chart content in defense against medical malpractice lawsuits.
main_findings: The content of the medical and hospital chart can support a defense or imperil the defense of the physician being sued. Aggrieved patients can pursue multiple theories of liability against obstetricians or gynecologists.
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported
future_research: Not reported
summary: The abstract discusses the importance of compassion, thorough attention to patients, and the role of medical and hospital chart content in defending against medical malpractice lawsuits. It also mentions that patients can pursue multiple theories of liability against obstetricians or gynecologists.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Anticoagulants in Patients With Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis: A Meta-Analysis.
research_objective: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of anticoagulants in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF)
main_findings: Anticoagulants did not significantly affect overall mortality in IPF patients. However, excluding studies with warfarin monotherapy, other anticoagulants extended patient survival. Anticoagulants improved lung function, increased lung capacity, and reduced plasma D-dimer levels. Anticoagulants were associated with significantly increased adverse events.
safety_information: Significantly increased adverse events (OR = 2.48, 95% CI [1.16, 5.32], p = 0.68)
explicit_limitations: Excluding studies with warfarin monotherapy
future_research: Further meta-analyses based on individual patient data are needed to confirm these findings
summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis found that anticoagulants may extend the lifespan of IPF patients and improve lung function, but they also increase the risk of adverse events such as bleeding.

title: Experimental models of epilepsy: A comprehensive review of mechanisms, translational relevance, and future directions.
research_objective: To summarize major experimental models of epilepsy and discuss their strengths, limitations, and translational relevance.
main_findings: The review discusses major experimental models of epilepsy, including chemically induced, electrically induced, and genetic approaches. It highlights the strengths, limitations, and translational relevance of these models, particularly in relation to human epilepsy subtypes such as generalized tonic-clonic and temporal lobe epilepsy. It also emphasizes the potential of advances in neuroimaging, omics technologies, and artificial intelligence-based analytics to enhance model accuracy and predictive validity. Ethical considerations, including the principles of replacement, reduction, and refinement, are also discussed.
explicit_limitations: Ethical considerations, including the principles of replacement, reduction, and refinement, are emphasized.
future_research: By integrating classical models with emerging technologies, this review provides a comprehensive framework to guide future research aimed at improving therapeutic strategies and bridging the gap between pre-clinical and clinical epilepsy research.
summary: This review summarizes major experimental models of epilepsy, their strengths, limitations, and translational relevance, and highlights the potential of emerging technologies to improve research in this field.

title: The Emerging Triad in Cancer and Aging: Cellular Senescence, Microbiome, and Tumor Microenvironment.
research_objective: To understand the multi-system processes of aging and their impact on various organ systems, including mitochondrial dysfunction, circadian disruption, hypoxia, inter-organ signaling, and cellular senescence.
main_findings: The articles in this special issue explore how these shared mechanisms of decline change across tissues and over time. They also highlight how systemic changes affect tissue-level dysfunction, particularly in vascular, immune, and metabolic systems. Several papers propose biomarkers and diagnostic strategies for earlier detection, risk stratification, and longitudinal monitoring of aging.
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported in the abstract
future_research: The issue emphasizes the need for further validation and integration of proposed tools to support clinical translation.
summary: This special issue examines the multi-system processes of aging, focusing on shared mechanisms like mitochondrial dysfunction and cellular senescence. It highlights the impact of these processes on various organ systems and proposes diagnostic tools for earlier detection and monitoring of aging.

title: Updated bowel preparation regimens for colonoscopy: benefits and drawbacks.
research_objective: To improve the effectiveness and patient compliance of bowel preparation for colonoscopy, particularly in terms of tolerability and adherence.
main_findings: The study reports on the efficacy and patient compliance of various bowel preparation regimens, including low- and ultralow-volume PEG-based regimens, oral sulfate solutions, and sodium picosulfate with magnesium citrate. The introduction of oral sulfate tablets has been noted for its efficacy and improved tolerability. Adjunctive simethicone has also been found to improve mucosal visibility.
efficacy_information: Noninferior efficacy compared to PEG-based regimens and comparable bowel-cleansing efficacy to other regimens.
safety_information: A few cases of gastric mucosal irritation have been reported with oral sulfate tablets, and adjunctive simethicone has been found to improve mucosal visibility.
explicit_limitations: A few cases of gastric mucosal irritation have been reported with oral sulfate tablets.
future_research: A personalized evidence-based approach, guided by patient-specific factors and supported by emerging clinical data, can improve adherence, ensure adequate bowel cleansing, and enhance the diagnostic yield and procedural efficiency of colonoscopy.
summary: The study evaluates various bowel preparation regimens for colonoscopy, highlighting the efficacy and patient compliance of low- and ultralow-volume PEG-based regimens, oral sulfate solutions, and sodium picosulfate with magnesium citrate. It also notes the benefits of adjunctive simethicone in improving mucosal visibility. The introduction of oral sulfate tablets has shown improved tolerability, but with a few reported cases of gastric mucosal irritation. Future research should focus on personalized approaches to optimize bowel preparation for better outcomes.

title: Advances in Drug Delivery Science for Diacerein: Strategies to Enhance Solubility, Bioavailability, and Pharmacokinetic Performance.
research_objective: To address the clinical limitations of diacerein, including poor aqueous solubility, low bioavailability, liver issues, and gastrointestinal side effects, particularly diarrhea, by exploring various innovative pharmaceutical formulation approaches.
main_findings: Progress in formulation approaches aimed at enhancing the solubility and therapeutic profile of diacerein, with special emphasis on lipid-based carriers, vesicular systems, pH-responsive hydrogels, and dissolving microneedles.
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported in the abstract
future_research: The insights presented here may also guide the development of more effective delivery systems for other poorly soluble anti-inflammatory agents.
summary: The abstract highlights advancements in formulating diacerein to improve its solubility and therapeutic profile, with a focus on lipid-based carriers, vesicular systems, pH-responsive hydrogels, and dissolving microneedles. These developments aim to overcome clinical limitations and improve patient outcomes.

title: Sex differences in immunotherapy plus chemotherapy: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
research_objective: To determine if biological sex affects the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitor plus chemotherapy regimens compared to chemotherapy alone in cancer patients.
main_findings: Combination therapy with immune checkpoint inhibitors plus chemotherapy significantly improved overall survival and progression-free survival in both male and female patients across various cancer types. The combination therapy provided 24% and 22% mortality reductions in males and females, respectively, with improvements of 39% and 34% in progression-free survival.
efficacy_information: Combination therapy with immune checkpoint inhibitors plus chemotherapy significantly improved overall survival and progression-free survival in both male and female patients across various cancer types.
explicit_limitations: No explicitly stated limitations in the abstract.
future_research: Recommendations for future research include continued sex-stratified data reporting in clinical trials to ensure equitable treatment access and to further understand the impact of sex on treatment outcomes.
summary: The study found that combining immune checkpoint inhibitors with chemotherapy provided significant and equivalent survival benefits for both male and female patients across various cancer types, suggesting that treatment decisions should be based on tumor characteristics rather than patient sex.

title: [Progresses on temporal interference electromagnetic stimulation for non-invasive deep brain function modulation].
research_objective: To analyze the fundamental principle of temporal interference (TI) electromagnetic stimulation for deep brain function modulation and its clinical applications, including motor symptoms in Parkinson's disease, working memory enhancement, and epileptic foci localization.
main_findings: The review reveals that TI offers superior focal specificity in deep brain regions compared with traditional transcranial electric or magnetic stimulation. Multi-electrode or multi-coil configurations can substantially enhance the focality and penetration of electric fields in deep brain areas. TI has shown potential advantages in improving motor symptoms in Parkinson's disease, enhancing working memory, and localizing epileptic foci.
efficacy_information: Improves motor symptoms in Parkinson's disease, enhances working memory, and localizes epileptic foci.
safety_information: Careful evaluation on TI's safety and ethical considerations remains essential.
explicit_limitations: Careful evaluation on TI's safety and ethical considerations remains essential.
future_research: Integrating artificial intelligence-based parameter optimization with personalized brain network modeling represents a key pathway toward overcoming current technical limitations.
summary: This systematic review highlights the potential of temporal interference (TI) electromagnetic stimulation for deep brain function modulation, particularly in improving motor symptoms in Parkinson's disease, enhancing working memory, and localizing epileptic foci. However, safety and ethical considerations need further evaluation, and integrating AI with personalized brain modeling is recommended for future research.

title: Targeting autophagy to enhance cancer immunotherapy: emerging mechanisms and strategies.
research_objective: To review the current understanding of autophagy's role in cancer and its potential as a therapeutic target to enhance antitumor immunity.
main_findings: The review discusses the dual role of autophagy in cancer, its influence on immune escape, and the need for a deeper mechanistic understanding to identify therapeutic targets. It also highlights emerging approaches to modulate autophagy in tumor and immune cells while preserving immune function.
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported in the abstract
future_research: The review suggests integrating insights from immuno-oncology and cellular metabolism to develop combinatorial strategies and facilitate the clinical translation of autophagy-targeted immunotherapies.
summary: This review summarizes the current understanding of autophagy in cancer and its potential as a therapeutic target, emphasizing the need for further research to identify selective targets and develop combinatorial strategies.

title: Cardiovascular Risk Through Hypoxic Burden in Children With Sleep Apnea: A Secondary Analysis of a Nonrandomized Clinical Trial.
research_objective: To explore whether hypoxic burden (HB) is associated with disturbances in blood pressure (BP) patterns in pediatric obstructive sleep apnea (OSA).
main_findings: Higher HB levels were associated with greater nocturnal diastolic BP, a reduced nocturnal decrease in mean BP, and an increased prevalence of a nondipping pattern (NDP) in children with OSA. Multivariable analysis showed an increased risk of NDP in the higher quartile of HB.
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported in the abstract
future_research: These results suggest the potential utility of HB as a biomarker for CV risk stratification and clinical management in the pediatric population with OSA. The authors recommend further studies to validate these findings and explore the clinical implications.
summary: The study found that higher HB levels in children with OSA were associated with increased nocturnal diastolic BP, reduced nocturnal BP decrease, and an increased prevalence of NDP. The authors suggest HB as a potential biomarker for CV risk stratification in pediatric OSA, recommending further research to validate these findings.

title: Intrathoracic hemocoagulase Bothrops atrox injection efficacy in thoracoscopic lung cancer surgery.
research_objective: To evaluate the impact of intrathoracic HBA injection on perioperative outcomes and coagulation in patients undergoing VATS.
main_findings: The HBA group had significantly lower intraoperative bleeding volume, surgery duration, postoperative hospital stay, drainage volume, and drainage time compared to the non-HBA group before propensity score matching. After matching, the HBA group still demonstrated a higher postoperative thrombin time (TT) and shorter postoperative hospital stays and drainage volume compared to the non-HBA group. Multivariate analysis revealed that HBA and preoperative TT were independent risk factors for prolonged postoperative TT.
efficacy_information: Intrathoracic HBA injection in VATS may reduce postoperative hospital stay and drainage volume, albeit with prolonged TT.
safety_information: The HBA group had higher rates of comorbidities, more postoperative complications, and worse pre- and postoperative coagulation functions.
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported
future_research: Monitoring coagulation function before and after surgery is necessary for patients receiving HBA during surgery.
summary: This study found that intrathoracic HBA injection in VATS can reduce postoperative hospital stay and drainage volume, but it also prolonged the postoperative thrombin time. The study recommends monitoring coagulation function before and after surgery for patients receiving HBA during surgery.

title: Advancements and challenges of ultrasound imaging in the management of thyroid-associated ophthalmopathy.
research_objective: To review the current status of ultrasound applications in thyroid-associated ophthalmopathy (TAO) and propose strategies for future research.
main_findings: The review highlights the advantages of ultrasound in diagnosing and managing TAO, particularly in early detection and monitoring of disease progression. It also identifies key challenges such as limited resolution for deep orbital structures and a lack of standardized protocols, which can lead to diagnostic inaccuracies. The paper proposes strategies for future research, including the analysis of ultrasound imaging data to develop biomarker stratification models and the integration of ultrasound elastography with deep learning to improve diagnostic precision.
explicit_limitations: The paper identifies key challenges such as limited resolution for deep orbital structures and a lack of standardized protocols, which can lead to diagnostic inaccuracies. It also proposes strategies for future research, including the analysis of ultrasound imaging data to develop biomarker stratification models and the integration of ultrasound elastography with deep learning to improve diagnostic precision.
future_research: The paper proposes strategies for future research, including the analysis of ultrasound imaging data to develop biomarker stratification models and the integration of ultrasound elastography with deep learning to improve diagnostic precision.
summary: The abstract reviews the current status of ultrasound applications in thyroid-associated ophthalmopathy, highlighting its advantages and identifying key challenges. It also suggests future research directions to improve diagnostic precision.

title: Understanding facilitators and barriers of HPV vaccination amongst adolescent boys and their parents in high-income countries through the social-ecological model: a scoping review.
research_objective: Identify barriers and facilitators to HPV vaccination for adolescent boys and their parents in high-income countries
main_findings: 54 facilitators and 120 barriers were identified for HPV vaccination for adolescent boys and their parents
safety_information: Concerns regarding vaccine safety and side effects were identified as key barriers
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported
future_research: Future education studies should comprise each domain of the social-ecological model to successfully implement HPV vaccination in adolescent boys
summary: This study identified 54 facilitators and 120 barriers to HPV vaccination for adolescent boys and their parents in high-income countries, with safety concerns being a key barrier. The authors suggest that future education programs should incorporate the social-ecological model to improve vaccination rates.

title: Efficacy and Safety of
research_objective: To assess the efficacy and safety of Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. lactis CKDB001 (LL) supplementation in mild cognitive impairment (MCI) in a 12-week clinical trial.
main_findings: LL supplementation resulted in significantly greater improvements than placebo in the Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale-Cognition 13 total score, the memory sub-score, reaction time for Part A of the Trail Making Test, and word/color reaction times on the Stroop test. Taxonomic and metabolomic profiling of fecal samples showed significantly greater changes in the relative abundance of beneficial microorganisms in the LL group, with the most pronounced shifts at the family (Lactobacillaceae, Bifidobacteriaceae) and genus (Lactobacillus) levels. LL supplementation was safe and well-tolerated, with no clinically relevant changes in laboratory findings or adverse events.
efficacy_information: The Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale-Cognition 13 total score, the memory sub-score, reaction time for Part A of the Trail Making Test, and word/color reaction times on the Stroop test.
safety_information: Safe and well-tolerated, with no clinically relevant changes in laboratory findings or adverse events.
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported in the abstract.
future_research: These findings suggest that LL supplementation may enhance cognitive function in MCI by modulating the gut-brain axis through effects on gut microbiota and related metabolites, and could serve as a safe functional food to support cognitive health.
summary: The clinical trial found that LL supplementation improved cognitive function in MCI patients, as evidenced by better performance on cognitive tests. The gut microbiota and metabolites were also affected, suggesting a potential mechanism. LL was found to be safe and well-tolerated.

title: The role of tumor microenvironment in regulating tumor cell dormancy.
research_objective: To provide novel insights for both mechanistic studies and therapeutic strategies aimed at inducing persistent dormancy or eradicating dormant cells to prevent tumor recurrence and metastasis
main_findings: The review discusses how the tumor microenvironment (TME) governs the entry, maintenance, and reactivation of dormant tumor cells, which are major causes of tumor-related deaths.
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported in the abstract
future_research: To provide novel insights for both mechanistic studies and therapeutic strategies aimed at inducing persistent dormancy or eradicating dormant cells to prevent tumor recurrence and metastasis
summary: The abstract discusses the role of the tumor microenvironment in controlling dormant tumor cells, which are responsible for tumor recurrence and metastasis, and suggests future research directions.

title: Review of ultrasonication-assisted Fenton processes for degrading aqueous pollutants.
research_objective: Examine the theoretical foundations, operational effectiveness, and recent developments associated with US/Fenton techniques in wastewater remediation.
main_findings: The US/Fenton technique enhances the generation of OH radicals, improving the degradation of resistant contaminants in wastewater. It involves ultrasonication with Fenton's reagent, and its effectiveness is influenced by factors such as ultrasonication frequency, energy input, pH, and reagent dosage. Novel adaptations like US/photo-Fenton and US/electro-Fenton are discussed, and their roles in sludge treatment and related applications are explored. The review also addresses current challenges and future research needs for the widespread implementation of US/Fenton.
efficacy_information: The US/Fenton technique enhances the generation of OH radicals, improving the degradation of resistant contaminants in wastewater.
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported in the abstract
future_research: Outlines future research needs for the widespread implementation of US/Fenton.
summary: This review examines the US/Fenton technique, highlighting its effectiveness in degrading resistant contaminants in wastewater and its potential for various applications. It also identifies future research areas to advance its use.

title: [Side effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors : Focus on pulmonary events].
research_objective: To analyze immune-mediated adverse events (iAEs) specifically in the context of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) therapy, with a focus on pulmonary iAEs.
main_findings: The paper discusses immune-mediated adverse events (iAEs) that can occur during therapy with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI), with a particular emphasis on pulmonary iAEs.
safety_information: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) are associated with less toxicity compared to chemotherapy, and iAEs may occur during therapy with ICI.
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported in the abstract
future_research: Not reported in the abstract
summary: The study highlights the occurrence of immune-mediated adverse events, particularly pulmonary iAEs, in patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors for cancer treatment.

title: Long-term comparative effectiveness of once-weekly semaglutide versus alternative treatments in a real-world US adult population with type 2 diabetes: a randomized pragmatic clinical trial.
research_objective: To evaluate the long-term effectiveness of once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide versus alternative treatment in adults with type 2 diabetes (T2D) in routine clinical practice.
main_findings: Participants randomized to semaglutide had significantly higher proportions achieving glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) <7.0% at both year 1 (53.1% vs 45.5%) and year 2 (49.9% vs 38.9%) compared to those on alternative treatment. Semaglutide also showed larger reductions in HbA1c, body weight, and patient-reported outcomes (PROs) compared to alternative treatment.
efficacy_information: Semaglutide was associated with a higher proportion of participants achieving HbA1c <7.0% at both year 1 and year 2, and with larger reductions in HbA1c, body weight, and PROs.
safety_information: No new safety concerns were identified with semaglutide.
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported
future_research: Findings support semaglutide as an effective and well-tolerated option in clinical practice, but future research is recommended to further explore the long-term safety and efficacy of semaglutide in this population.
summary: The study found that semaglutide was more effective than alternative treatments in achieving glycemic control and reducing body weight in adults with type 2 diabetes, supporting its use in clinical practice. No new safety concerns were identified, but further research is recommended.

title: Digital Innovations for Managing Sleep Problems in Adolescents.
research_objective: Synthesize the current literature on assessment, treatment, and digital interventions for adolescent sleep problems
main_findings: Key challenges and areas for future research in the field of adolescent sleep are identified
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported in the abstract
future_research: Recommendations for future research are provided
summary: The abstract highlights the need for further research to address the challenges in assessing, treating, and developing digital interventions for adolescent sleep problems.

title: [Endoscope for the diagnosis and treatment of ear diseases].
research_objective: The evolving and increasing role of endoscopes in ear examination and treatment of ear diseases, including ear surgery.

research_objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of a community-based eye health promotion program in improving preventive eye health behaviors and vision-related quality of life among Thai older persons.
main_findings: The intervention group showed a statistically significant improvement in preventive eye health behavior scores by 0.207 points at 8 weeks, increasing to 0.376 points at 12 weeks, compared to the comparison group. title: Advances of Drug-Loaded Microsphere Technology for Targeted Immunotherapy Against Prostate Cancer.
research_objective: To review the use of microcatheter-assisted techniques for precise embolization using drug-loaded microspheres combined with immunotherapy and targeted therapy in treating advanced prostate cancer.
main_findings: The review discusses the use of microcatheter-assisted techniques for precise embolization using drug-loaded microspheres combined with immunotherapy and targeted therapy in treating advanced prostate cancer. summary: The review discusses the use of microcatheter-assisted techniques for precise embolization using drug-loaded microspheres combined with immunotherapy and targeted therapy in treating advanced prostate cancer, reporting efficacy and safety data, and highlighting the need for future research to standardize protocols and validate long-term outcomes.

title: An intranasal adjuvanted, recombinant influenza A/H5 vaccine primes against diverse H5N1 clades: a phase I trial.
research_objective: To evaluate the safety and immunogenicity of a recombinant influenza A/H5 (A/Indonesia/05/2005, clade 2.1) hemagglutinin vaccine formulated with a nanoemulsion adjuvant administered intranasally in two doses.
main_findings: The vaccine is well tolerated. After the intranasal series, hemagglutination inhibition and microneutralization responses are minimal. However, adjuvanted H5 recipients show significant increases in mucosal and serum IgG/IgA, surface plasmon resonance antibody binding, memory B and CD4 T cell activity, and antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity. Following H5N1 boost, participants mount robust responses across measurements and have microneutralization responses against diverse H5N1 clades (including circulating clade 2.3.4.4b).
efficacy_information: Findings demonstrate successful mucosal priming and broad cross-clade responses. This intranasal vaccine supports further exploration of mucosal immune biomarkers and may accelerate development of intranasal influenza vaccines.
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported in the abstract.
future_research: This intranasal vaccine supports further exploration of mucosal immune biomarkers and may accelerate development of intranasal influenza vaccines.
summary: The study evaluated a novel influenza vaccine and found that while it was well-tolerated, it did not induce strong immune responses. However, it showed promise in priming the immune system for mucosal responses and cross-clade protection, suggesting potential for further research and development.

title: The role of deer keds (Diptera: Hippoboscidae: Lipoptena and Neolipoptena) in occupational and public health.
research_objective: To summarize recent knowledge regarding the health risks posed by deer keds, applicable to both occupational groups and anyone who may encounter them within their geographic distribution.
main_findings: Deer keds are bloodsucking arthropods that can feed on deer and occasionally bite humans. They have been detected as potential vectors for various infectious disease agents, including Bartonella schoenbuchensis. They are found in forests and their immediate surroundings in the Northern Hemisphere, particularly in temperate regions of Europe, Siberia, China, and North America. Climate change is expected to favor the spread of deer keds.
safety_information: Measures to prevent bites include avoiding areas with high occurrences of deer keds, wearing protective clothing, conducting a thorough body check for deer keds and bite sites, and educating at-risk workers and those recreating in forests about deer ked bites, their symptoms, and possible zoonotic implications.
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported in the abstract
future_research: Not reported in the abstract
summary: This review summarizes the recent knowledge about the health risks posed by deer keds, which are bloodsucking arthropods found in forests and their surroundings in the Northern Hemisphere. They have been detected as vectors for various infectious diseases and are expected to spread with climate change. Measures to prevent bites include avoiding high-risk areas, wearing protective clothing, and educating at-risk workers and recreational users about deer ked bites and their implications.

title: Fibrin glue versus sutures for securing conjunctival autograft in primary pterygium surgery: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
research_objective: To evaluate whether fibrin glue provides superior outcomes compared to sutures for securing conjunctival autografts in primary pterygium surgery, focusing on recurrence rates, operative time, postoperative complications, and patient discomfort.
main_findings: Fibrin glue significantly reduced recurrence risk compared to sutures (pooled odds ratio: 2.46; 95% CI: 1.06-5.69; 27 P = .0352; I2 = 0%). Operative time was significantly shorter with fibrin glue (pooled mean difference: 15.65 minutes; 95% CI: 11.45-19.86; P < .005; I2 = 99.29%). Pain scores at postoperative day 1 were significantly lower with fibrin glue compared to sutures (pooled standardized mean difference: 1.32; 95% CI: -2.11 to -0.52; p < .001; I2 = 90%).
efficacy_information: Fibrin glue is associated with lower recurrence rates, reduced operative time, and less postoperative discomfort.
safety_information: Subconjunctival hemorrhages were more common in the suture group.
explicit_limitations: Variability in graft retraction outcomes warrants further investigation.
future_research: Further investigation into graft retraction outcomes is recommended.
summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis found that fibrin glue is associated with lower recurrence rates, reduced operative time, and less postoperative discomfort compared to sutures in primary pterygium surgery. However, further research is needed to investigate graft retraction outcomes.

title: A Comparative Overview of Technological Advances in Fall Detection Systems for Elderly People.

main_findings: The review found a predominance in the use of inertial systems (accelerometers and gyroscopes) due to their low cost and wide availability. However, approaches combining image analysis with artificial intelligence and machine learning algorithms show superiority in terms of accuracy and robustness. Progress has also been made in the development of multisensory solutions based on IoT technologies, which integrate information from various sources to optimize real-time decision-making.
efficacy_information: The review did not report on the efficacy of these solutions in terms of their effectiveness in detecting falls.
safety_information: The review did not report on the safety of these solutions.
explicit_limitations: The review did not explicitly state any limitations of the solutions.
future_research: The review did not provide recommendations for future research.
summary: This scoping review identified the use of inertial systems as the most prevalent technology for fall detection in older adults, but also highlighted the superiority of approaches combining image analysis with AI and machine learning for accuracy and robustness. The review also noted advancements in multisensory IoT solutions for real-time decision-making.
