title: Post-Event Strategies for Workplace Violence Affecting Hospital Staff: A Scoping Review.
research_objective: To map the evidence on post-incident strategies for workplace violence in global hospital settings, define current literature gaps and provide direction for future research.
main_findings: Twenty-seven articles were included in the review, addressing post-violence strategies for staff support, behaviour management of aggressors, and system-level responses. These strategies are typically embedded within larger multicomponent workplace violence programmes, with limited disaggregation of their specific effects.
efficacy_information: Most articles in the review equated success with violence reduction, reflecting a traditional focus on risk mitigation.
explicit_limitations: The evidence base for tertiary prevention of workplace violence remains sparse.
future_research: Future research and service improvement initiatives should focus more closely on outcomes relevant to staff experiences. Incorporating a Safety-II perspective could enable hospitals to strengthen ongoing operational capabilities in the aftermath of violence and help to redress the conditions that facilitate its recurrence.
summary: The review identified 27 articles on post-incident strategies for workplace violence in hospitals, highlighting support for staff, behaviour management of aggressors, and system-level responses. However, the evidence base is limited, and future research should prioritize outcomes for frontline staff and adopt a broader perspective on workplace violence.

title: Cardiovascular disease in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies.
research_objective: To quantify the magnitudes of association between idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) and both overall and specific categories of cardiovascular (CV) disease.
main_findings: The review found a positive association between IPF and CV disease, with pooled odds ratios (OR) and relative risks (RR) indicating increased risks for various CV conditions such as ischemic heart disease, thromboembolic disease, pulmonary hypertension, and other forms of heart disease.
explicit_limitations: Meta-regression and maximized subgroup analyses confirmed the influence of control characteristics, data source, Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) score, certainty of CV disease diagnosis, body mass index (BMI), smoking status, and diabetes prevalence on both heterogeneity and risk estimates in the case-control/cross-sectional datasets.
future_research: The authors recommended systematic screening and risk reduction strategies in IPF patients, emphasizing the need for further research.
summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis found a significant association between idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and various cardiovascular diseases, highlighting the need for improved screening and risk reduction strategies in IPF patients.

title: Phase 1 dose escalation trial of the selective adenosine A2B antagonist PBF-1129 in patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer.
research_objective: To evaluate the safety and efficacy of PBF-1129, an oral, selective A2B adenosine receptor (A2BAR) antagonist, in patients with advanced/metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) who had progressed on standard therapies.
main_findings: PBF-1129 was well-tolerated with no dose-limiting toxicities observed. Best response was stable disease in 3 out of 21 patients, including 2 of 6 treated at the recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D). Immunophenotyping showed post-treatment reductions in programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) expression on CD8⁺ T cells, which correlated with improved survival. Reductions in PD-1 expression on CD4⁺ T cells and decreased myeloid-derived suppressor cells were also associated with better outcomes. PBF-1129 showed dose-proportional pharmacokinetics and maintained plasma concentrations above the 90% maximal inhibitory concentration (IC90) of A2BAR at 320 mg for 24 h.
efficacy_information: Best response was stable disease in 3 out of 21 patients, including 2 of 6 treated at the recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D). Immunophenotyping showed post-treatment reductions in programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) expression on CD8⁺ T cells, which correlated with improved survival. Reductions in PD-1 expression on CD4⁺ T cells and decreased myeloid-derived suppressor cells were also associated with better outcomes.
safety_information: No dose-limiting toxicities observed. The most frequently reported treatment-related adverse events were lymphocytopenia, vomiting, anorexia, and fatigue.

title: Real-world evaluation of MRI fistula volume as a radiological biomarker of disease activity in perianal fistulizing Crohn's disease.
research_objective: To evaluate MRI fistula volume as a radiological biomarker and its longitudinal association with perianal fistulizing Crohn's disease (pfCD) class.
main_findings: MRI fistula volume is associated with disease severity and disease trajectory in perianal fistulizing Crohn's disease (pfCD). Volume thresholds are associated with classification shifts and clinical response, supporting their potential as objective quantitative tools.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Urolithiasis Imaging and Intervention: A Narrative Review of Current Applications, Barriers, and Future Directions.
research_objective: Examine the state of artificial intelligence (AI) applications in urolithiasis and their impact on treatment planning and diagnostic accuracy.
main_findings: AI models are improving the accuracy of computed tomography (CT) and ultrasonography (US) in diagnosing urolithiasis. They provide automatic stone detection, precise stone burden calculation, and assistance in differentiating difficult mimics. Sophisticated algorithms and radiomics are demonstrating promise in determining stone composition preoperatively. AI models are also improving the prediction of the success of procedures like extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy (ESWL) and percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL).
explicit_limitations: The need for large datasets and ensuring models are reliable and generalizable across different clinical settings.
future_research: Developing best-practice guidelines, robust training programs, and strong interdisciplinary collaboration.
summary: This study examines AI applications in urolithiasis, highlighting improvements in diagnostic accuracy and treatment prediction. However, significant challenges remain, particularly in data availability and model reliability.

Initial studies suggest these therapies can improve insulin secretion, assist pancreatic beta cell preservation, enhance insulin-mediated glucose metabolism, reduce glucagon secretion, and reduce the risk of fatty liver disease.
efficacy_information: Improvement in glycaemic control, insulin secretion, pancreatic beta cell preservation, and glucose metabolism; reduction in glucagon secretion and risk of fatty liver disease.

summary: The review discusses promising non-insulin therapies for type 2 diabetes, including incretin-based and amylin-based synthetic peptides, antibodies, and agents modulating mitochondrial function and receptors. These therapies show potential for improving glycaemic control, insulin secretion, and reducing the risk of fatty liver disease.

title: A preventive care strategy to reduce moderate or severe acute kidney injury after major surgery (BigpAK-2); a multinational, randomised clinical trial.
research_objective: To identify patients at high risk of acute kidney injury (AKI) using urinary biomarkers and to implement a preventive care strategy to reduce AKI within 72 hours after major surgery.
main_findings: The preventive care strategy significantly reduced the occurrence of moderate or severe AKI (14.4% in the intervention group vs 22.3% in the control group) without increasing adverse events.

explicit_limitations: The study was conducted in 34 hospitals in Europe and the results may not be generalizable to other settings.

summary: This study found that a preventive care strategy reduced the occurrence of moderate or severe AKI after major surgery, without increasing adverse events, but the results may not be generalizable to other settings.

title: Clinical Efficacy and Safety of BIC/TAF/FTC in Elderly HIV-Infected Individuals in Southwest China: A Retrospective Observation Study.
research_objective: To evaluate the real-world effectiveness and safety of the bictegravir emtricitabine tenofovir alafenamide fumarate (B/F/TAF) regimen in elderly HIV-infected individuals in southwest China.
main_findings: The B/F/TAF regimen achieved a high viral suppression rate (93.1% in the treatment-naïve group and 92.9% in the treatment-experienced group) at 48 weeks. explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported in the abstract.
future_research: The metabolic effects of BIC/FTC/TAF in untreated patients require longer follow-up.

title: Advancing Medulloblastoma Treatment: Molecular Mechanisms, Drug Repurposing, and Precision Therapies.
research_objective: To improve treatment outcomes for high-risk medulloblastoma subtypes, particularly Group 3, and to explore new therapeutic strategies that reduce toxicity and improve patient quality of life.
main_findings: Advances in molecular diagnostics have improved the subclassification of medulloblastomas. However, treatment outcomes for high-risk subtypes, particularly Group 3, remain poor. Effective drug delivery across the blood-brain barrier is a major challenge. Drug repurposing using FDA-approved agents like niclosamide, itraconazole, and arsenic trioxide shows promise but faces challenges such as limited blood-brain barrier penetration and lack of pediatric-specific pharmacokinetic data.
explicit_limitations: Challenges such as limited blood-brain barrier penetration and the lack of pediatric-specific pharmacokinetic data persist.

Emerging technologies, including nanotechnology-based delivery systems, CRISPR-mediated gene editing, and chimeric antigen receptor-T cell therapies, hold significant potential but require further refinement to address toxicity, off-target effects, and biomarker development.
summary: The abstract highlights the need for improved treatment strategies for high-risk medulloblastoma subtypes, particularly Group 3, and emphasizes the challenges in effective drug delivery and toxicity. It also suggests future research directions in personalized therapy, drug delivery systems, and emerging technologies.

title: Targeting TWEAK/Fn14 pathway: Implications for stem cell regulation and advancements in skin disease therapies.
research_objective: To examine the dual roles of TWEAK/Fn14 signaling in skin disease pathogenesis and stem cell regulation, and to highlight its potential as a diagnostic biomarker and therapeutic target.
main_findings: TWEAK/Fn14 signaling is implicated in fibroproliferation, angiogenesis, and inflammation in skin disorders. It is upregulated in the serum and urine of patients with conditions like lupus erythematosus, psoriasis, and skin tumors. Moderate activation promotes skin wound healing, while prolonged or excessive activation may lead to pathological tissue damage. Beyond skin diseases, TWEAK/Fn14 signaling influences the behavior of various stem cells, including liver, neural, and mesenchymal stem cells, modulating their proliferation and differentiation during tissue repair and regeneration.
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported in the abstract
future_research: The review suggests potential for TWEAK/Fn14 signaling as a diagnostic biomarker and therapeutic target, and recommends further research into its mechanisms and applications in disease mechanisms, stem cell therapy, and tissue engineering.
summary: This review highlights the dual roles of TWEAK/Fn14 signaling in skin diseases and stem cell regulation, suggesting its potential as a diagnostic biomarker and therapeutic target. It also underscores the need for further research in these areas.

title: Next-Generation Proteolysis-Targeting Chimeras in Precision Oncology: Multifunctional Designs, Emerging Modalities, and Translational Prospects in Targeted Protein Degradation.
research_objective: To provide a critical overview of the design rationales, molecular mechanisms of action, therapeutic utilities, and synthetic issues associated with innovative PROTAC platforms, focusing on their translational implications and pharmacokinetic limitations, as well as potential future clinical applications.
main_findings: The review discusses next-generation PROTAC platforms, including dual-targeting PROTACS, TF-PROTACs, PhosphoTACs, and PhosTACs, which represent a paradigm shift from traditional enzyme inhibition to selective protein degradation. It highlights the potential of PROTACs in addressing resistance mechanisms and carcinogenic drivers in kinase degradation. Additionally, it covers the development of bio-responsive and spatially controlled PROTAC systems, such as photocaged and folate-caged PROTACs, and the clinical trials of ARV-110 and ARV-471.
efficacy_information: The review suggests that PROTACs have shown promise in addressing resistance mechanisms and carcinogenic drivers in kinase degradation.
explicit_limitations: Issues with clinical pharmacokinetics, E3 ligase tissue selectivity, and subcellular localization persist.
future_research: The review recommends the development of bio-responsive and spatially controlled PROTAC systems and the potential future clinical applications of PROTACs.
summary: This review discusses the next-generation PROTAC platforms and their potential in addressing resistance mechanisms and carcinogenic drivers, highlighting both their promise and limitations. It also suggests future research directions in this field.

title: Clinical ultrasound for the characterisation of obesity: beyond the body mass index.
research_objective: To evaluate the use of clinical ultrasound in the comprehensive evaluation of patients with obesity, particularly in relation to cardiovascular risk, renal dysfunction, hepatic steatosis, frailty, and hospital-related complications.
main_findings: Clinical ultrasound enables the direct and reproducible characterization of major fat compartments in patients with obesity, including epicardial, hepatic, perirenal, subcutaneous, and intramuscular fat. These measurements are associated with various health outcomes such as cardiovascular risk, renal dysfunction, hepatic steatosis, frailty, and hospital-related complications, even among individuals with normal weight. Ultrasound can also monitor changes in these fat compartments following therapeutic interventions.
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported in the abstract
future_research: Not reported in the abstract
summary: The abstract highlights the use of clinical ultrasound in evaluating obesity-related health outcomes, including cardiovascular risk, renal dysfunction, hepatic steatosis, and frailty, even in individuals with normal weight. It emphasizes the technique's accessibility, low cost, and prognostic value in internal medicine settings.

title: Trapeziectomy Versus Carpometacarpal Arthroplasty for Basilar Thumb Arthritis: A Narrative Review of Comparative Outcomes.
research_objective: Compare trapeziectomy-based procedures and CMC arthroplasty for treating thumb carpometacarpal (CMC) joint osteoarthritis.
main_findings: Both trapeziectomy-based procedures and CMC arthroplasty achieve excellent outcomes, with arthroplasty offering earlier functional gains but higher implant-specific complications and revision rates. Trapeziectomy remains a durable, cost-effective, and predictable treatment option.
efficacy_information: Both trapeziectomy-based procedures and CMC arthroplasty achieve excellent outcomes.
safety_information: Arthroplasty offers higher implant-specific complications and revision rates.
explicit_limitations: Individualized patient selection and shared decision-making are emphasized, and long-term comparative studies are needed to refine surgical guidelines.
future_research: Long-term comparative studies are needed to refine surgical guidelines.
summary: This review compares trapeziectomy-based procedures and CMC arthroplasty for thumb carpometacarpal (CMC) joint osteoarthritis, finding both to be effective with trapeziectomy being durable and cost-effective. Arthroplasty offers earlier functional gains but has higher complications and revision rates. Future research is needed to refine surgical guidelines.

title: Redefining fatty liver as metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: Implications of nomenclature changes for patients with diabetes.
research_objective: To explore the rationale behind the change from non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), compare diagnostic criteria, and evaluate the impact of the MASLD framework on disease prevalence, characterization, and outcomes in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) patients.
main_findings: The MASLD criteria include all individuals with T2DM and hepatic steatosis, emphasizing metabolic dysfunction as the primary driver. The MASLD framework identifies a higher prevalence of steatotic liver disease, particularly among T2DM patients, compared to NAFLD. The MASLD framework also introduces metabolic and alcohol-associated liver disease to account for dual etiologies involving alcohol use, which is common in T2DM populations but previously excluded under NAFLD criteria.
explicit_limitations: The new definitions highlight challenges such as unrecognized medication-induced steatosis and the need for reclassification in ongoing T2DM clinical trials.
future_research: Emerging evidence supports enhanced screening strategies (e.g., fibrosis-4) and metabolic-targeted treatments for MASLD in T2DM patients. The successful integration of MASLD into clinical practice will require system-wide reeducation, standardization, and multidisciplinary collaboration to improve outcomes for T2DM patients.
summary: This minireview explores the rationale behind the change from NAFLD to MASLD, emphasizing metabolic dysfunction as the primary driver. The MASLD framework identifies a higher prevalence of steatotic liver disease in T2DM patients, including those with alcohol-induced steatosis. Future research should focus on developing enhanced screening strategies and metabolic-targeted treatments for MASLD in T2DM patients.

title: Impact of intensive versus higher blood pressure control on cerebral blood flow in hypertension: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
research_objective: To classify SBP control into four threshold ranges and elucidate the differential effects of long-term SBP management on CBF dynamics.
main_findings: The meta-analysis included 12 randomized controlled trials (RCTs) with 1100 participants. SBP control, both acute and long-term, improved CBF with moderate robustness. Long-term SBP control improved CBF with low robustness, and intensive SBP control (120-129 mmHg) significantly increased long-term CBF with low heterogeneity and high robustness. Intensive SBP control showed a nonsignificant improvement in CBF compared with standard SBP control, but demonstrated a promising effect size.
efficacy_information: SBP control, both acute and long-term, improved CBF with moderate robustness. Long-term SBP control improved CBF with low robustness. Intensive SBP control (120-129 mmHg) significantly increased long-term CBF with low heterogeneity and high robustness.
explicit_limitations: Four long-term trials (33.33%) were identified as high risk with attrition bias due to dropout rates exceeding 20%. Long-term SBP control improved CBF with low robustness, due to the change of P value when removing a large-sample trial.
future_research: This review suggests that intensive SBP control might provide a potential advantage on CBF improvement and deceleration of cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) development, and might affect cognitive function but requires further verification in the hypertensive population.
summary: This study found that both acute and long-term SBP control improved CBF, with intensive SBP control (120-129 mmHg) showing a significant and promising effect on CBF improvement. However, long-term SBP control improved CBF with low robustness. Further research is needed to verify these findings and explore the potential benefits of intensive SBP control.

title: Achondroplasia treatments in children aged 5 and older.
research_objective: To review and highlight three investigational agents for the treatment of achondroplasia, a genetic disorder causing disproportionate short stature and multisystem complications.
main_findings: Clinical trials in children aged 5 years and older have shown that Vosoritide, Infigratinib, and Navepegritide improve annualized growth velocity compared to baseline. Safety profiles are favorable with few to no significant treatment-related adverse events reported. Available data suggest all three therapies bring growth trajectories of children with achondroplasia closer to unaffected peers.
efficacy_information: Improved annualized growth velocity with Vosoritide (1.7 cm/year), Infigratinib (6.0 cm/year), and Navepegritide (5.4 cm/year) compared to baseline.
safety_information: Favorable safety profiles with few to no significant treatment-related adverse events reported in the trials reviewed.
explicit_limitations: Direct comparisons across trials are limited, and long-term outcomes, particularly regarding comorbidities such as foramen magnum stenosis, spinal stenosis, and sleep apnea, remain under investigation.
future_research: Recommendations for future research include head-to-head studies and evaluation of combination strategies to optimize efficacy and durability.
summary: This review highlights three investigational agents for achondroplasia, a genetic disorder causing disproportionate short stature and multisystem complications. Clinical trials have shown promising efficacy and safety profiles, but long-term outcomes and combination strategies are under investigation.

title: Advances in the pharmaceutical development of antibody-oligonucleotide conjugates.
research_objective: To summarize the history and current clinical development of Antibody-Oligonucleotide Conjugates (AOCs), focusing on mechanisms of action, molecular design with various linkers, and recent advances in manufacturing processes and quality control.
main_findings: The review highlights the steady progress of AOCs in the early stages of development, emphasizing their potential to achieve targeted and efficient therapeutic intervention across various diseases. It also underscores the need for strategies to ensure therapeutic efficacy and minimize off-target toxicity, as well as the importance of design, manufacturing, and quality control in ensuring safety and efficacy.
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported in the abstract
future_research: Highlights current challenges and future prospects for the development of AOC therapeutics.
summary: This review summarizes the progress and challenges in the development of Antibody-Oligonucleotide Conjugates (AOCs), emphasizing their potential for targeted therapeutic intervention and the need for ongoing research in manufacturing and quality control.

title: Multiple Renal Arteries in Renal Transplantation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
research_objective: To identify the complications and outcomes associated with the use of renal transplants with multiple renal arteries (MRA) when compared to single renal arteries (SRA)
main_findings: Live-donor graft survival at 1 year and 5 years was significantly lower in the MRA group compared to the SRA group. Total complication rates were significantly higher in the MRA group for both live and deceased donors. Vascular complication rates from live donors and deceased donors both favored the SRA group. Live-donor patient survival at 1 year favored the MRA group.
safety_information: Reported safety findings include increased total complications and vascular complications in the MRA group, with some benefits in live donor survival.
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported
future_research: Recommendations for future research include considering MRA grafts based on patient/donor and anatomical factors, and further studies on living donor MRA.
summary: This meta-analysis found that MRA grafts have lower survival rates and higher complication rates compared to SRA grafts, but live donor survival is slightly better. The authors suggest considering MRA grafts based on patient and donor factors, and further research is needed.

title: Comprehensive guide to the diagnosis, management, and treatment of metastatic spinal cord compression syndrome.
research_objective: To propose a diagnosis and treatment algorithm for patients with metastatic spinal cord compression syndrome based on individualization and joint management by a multidisciplinary team.
main_findings: The most common symptom is back pain, which appears in up to 95% of patients with spinal cord compression syndrome. Treatment for spinal cord compression syndrome involves pain control with analgesic medications and the use of steroids, primarily dexamethasone, which has demonstrated efficacy and safety. Radiotherapy is essential for both definitive and complementary treatment, and metastatic spinal surgery is considered part of the definitive treatment, especially for unstable patients.
efficacy_information: The efficacy and safety of dexamethasone in pain control have been demonstrated in the context of patients with spinal cord compression syndrome.
safety_information: The use of dexamethasone has been reported to be safe in the context of patients with spinal cord compression syndrome.
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported in the abstract.
future_research: Not reported in the abstract.
summary: The abstract discusses the common symptoms, treatment options, and the importance of multidisciplinary management for patients with metastatic spinal cord compression syndrome, emphasizing the role of pain control with dexamethasone and the necessity of individualized radiotherapy and surgical approaches.

title: The Neuromuscular Junction: A Shared Vulnerability in Aging and Disease.
research_objective: To highlight shared and disease-specific mechanisms contributing to neuromuscular junction (NMJ) impairment in conditions such as amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, congenital myasthenic syndromes, autoimmune disorders, and sarcopenia, and to discuss emerging molecular drivers of NMJ dysfunction.
main_findings: Shared and disease-specific mechanisms contributing to NMJ impairment are discussed, including presynaptic, postsynaptic, and perisynaptic Schwann cell defects. Age-related changes at the NMJ are also emphasized. Emerging molecular drivers of NMJ dysfunction are explored, particularly in congenital myasthenic syndromes, autoimmune disorders, and advanced omics approaches. Promising interventions targeting presynaptic neurotransmitter release, postsynaptic excitability, and perisynaptic Schwann cells are discussed as avenues to improve neuromuscular transmission and maintain muscle strength.
explicit_limitations: Not explicitly reported in the abstract
future_research: Promising interventions targeting presynaptic neurotransmitter release, postsynaptic excitability, and perisynaptic Schwann cells are discussed as avenues to improve neuromuscular transmission and maintain muscle strength. The challenges and opportunities in translating these mechanistic insights into clinical therapies are also discussed. Novel human neuromuscular organoid models and advanced molecular profiling are highlighted as tools to bridge this gap.
summary: The abstract emphasizes the importance of the neuromuscular junction (NMJ) in various neuromuscular diseases and aging, highlighting shared and disease-specific mechanisms contributing to NMJ impairment. It also discusses emerging molecular drivers of NMJ dysfunction and promising interventions to improve neuromuscular transmission and maintain muscle strength.

title: Exploring the Use of Robotics in Reconstructive and Plastic Surgery: A Comprehensive Perspective.
research_objective: To critically appraise the contemporary literature on robot-assisted surgery (RAS) in plastic and reconstructive surgery, exploring its risks, benefits, limitations, and challenges.
main_findings: The current literature suggests that RAS is comparable, if not superior, to conventional techniques with respect to safety and effectiveness in specific reconstructive procedures. Reported benefits include shorter hospital stays, fewer complications, improved cosmetic outcomes, and enhanced surgeon dexterity. Challenges persist, such as steep learning curves, high acquisition and maintenance costs, and a lack of tactile feedback.
efficacy_information: Comparable, if not superior, to conventional techniques with respect to safety and effectiveness in specific reconstructive procedures.
safety_information: Steep learning curves, high acquisition and maintenance costs, and a lack of tactile feedback are reported challenges.
explicit_limitations: Steep learning curves, high acquisition and maintenance costs, and a lack of tactile feedback are reported challenges.
future_research: Future research should prioritize high-quality comparative trials, cost-effectiveness analyses, and training programs to facilitate broader clinical integration.
summary: The current literature indicates that RAS is comparable to conventional techniques in terms of safety and effectiveness for specific reconstructive procedures, with benefits including shorter hospital stays and improved outcomes. However, challenges such as steep learning curves, high costs, and lack of tactile feedback persist, necessitating further research and training programs.
